firmographic.name: Clay
firmographic.company_description:
Clay (legal entity: Clay Labs Inc.) is an AI-native go-to-market (GTM) development platform headquartered in New York City, founded in 2017 and operating under CEO Kareem Amin and co-founder Varun Anand. The company combines a 150+ provider waterfall enrichment marketplace, a proprietary AI research agent (Claygent, executing ~140M runs per month), a natural-language AI co-pilot (Sculptor), an intent and signals engine, a native email sequencer (Sequencer), code-based extensibility (Clay Functions), and a Model Context Protocol server (Clay MCP) that exposes its workflows to external AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Codex. Its core product surface is the Clay table, which unifies data, AI, signals, and orchestration into a single workflow environment used by sales, marketing, and RevOps teams.

Clay serves primarily B2B sales, RevOps, and GTM engineering personas across enterprise customers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Canva, Rippling, Intercom, Notion, Figma, Verkada), mid-market accounts (Vanta, Pendo, Hex, Merge), and a long tail of startups and SMBs, supported by a 40,000+ member community, Clay University, the annual Sculpt conference, and a certified Clay Studio Partner channel (demandDrive, Cobalt Keys). The company monetizes through tiered SaaS subscriptions (Launch at $185/mo, Advanced at $495/mo, custom Enterprise contracts), usage-based consumption on Data Credits and Actions, and partner-influenced revenue. Following its August 2025 $100M Series C at a $3.1B valuation, Clay reported approximately $100M ARR in December 2025, with net retention above 200%, and reached a $5B valuation via a January 2026 employee tender offer; the company is also expanding its Manhattan headquarters with a $50M R&D commitment and 498 new jobs.

recent_move.description: Closed a $100M Series C led by CapitalG at a $3.1B valuation in August 2025, bringing total funding to approximately $204M and providing capital to scale the GTM engineering category.

Launched six major platform products at Sculpt 2025 in September 2025: Sculptor AI co-pilot, Claygent Builder, Claygent Connectors, Audiences, Sequencer, and Web Intent, extending Clay from enrichment to full GTM orchestration.

Clay announced it will significantly expand its Manhattan headquarters by leasing 163,095 square feet of office space at 11 Madison Avenue in the Flatiron District, with plans to create 498 new full-time jobs over five years and invest $50 million in research and development activity in New York State, supported by up to $9.96 million in Excelsior Jobs Program tax credits from Empire State Development.
recent_move.title: NYC Headquarters Expansion

expansion_highlight.description: NYC expansion plan tied to 498 new jobs over five years alongside a $50M R&D investment commitment, announced April 2026, signals aggressive organizational scaling.

Sculpt 2025 introduced six new products (Sculptor, Claygent Builder, Claygent Connectors, Audiences, Sequencer, Web Intent) and early-2026 added Clay Functions and Clay MCP, expanding the platform from data enrichment into full GTM workflow orchestration and AI agent distribution.

EMEA-specific data partnerships with Lusha (verified phone, EMEA-compliant data, March 2026), Beauhurst (UK/Germany funding data, March 2026), and Ocean.io, plus GDPR/CCPA compliance, indicate a deliberate push into European markets.
Clay Partner Program launched August 2025 with solution, integration, creator, and startup tiers, formalizing the indirect sales channel alongside Clay Studio Partners demandDrive and Cobalt Keys.

January 2025 acquisition of Avenue (intent signal workflow automation) and acquisition of The Kiln (now part of 2X, a Clay Studio Partner) suggest continued tuck-in M&A to deepen agent and agency capacity.

March 2026 pricing restructure separating Data Credits (company/people data) and Actions (enrichments, AI tasks, workflow operations) with advanced features moved behind a $495/month tier is designed to capture more value from heavy-usage enterprise accounts.
Raised approximately $204M across disclosed rounds through August 2025, with two tender offers (Sept 2025 at $1.5B, Jan 2026 at $5B), sustaining primary capital availability for continued expansion.
